meta.title: The Dungeon Door Map Procedure (original random dungeon generator)
meta.srd: original (trap and hazard targets are SRD)
meta.attribution: Original procedure dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. Trap and hazard entries point at SRD 5.1 and SRD 5.2 material already attributed in those files.
meta.notes: Authored for The Dungeon Door to fill the gap left by the copyrighted DMG Appendix A random dungeon tables, which are not in the SRD and were not copied or closely paraphrased. The Basic Fantasy RPG 'Dungeon Generator' supplement (OGL 1.0a, Roberto Bisceglie, 2021) is another open mapping procedure, but a complete copy could not be retrieved here (the publisher's downloads returned 403). Prefer this graph procedure for the 5e server; see also extras/oseDungeonStocking.json for an open old-school stocking table.

records.name: The Dungeon Door Map Procedure
records.purpose: A seeded, graph-based way to build a small 5e adventure map (about 5 to 9 rooms) for The Dungeon Door. It is not a geomorphic 'draw the next 30-foot passage' generator and is not adapted from the 2014 or 1e DMG Appendix A tables.

seeding.description: All rolls use a deterministic RNG seeded from the adventure id (for example the party door code plus the adventure name). The same seed always yields the same map, which keeps tests and replays stable.

steps: 1. Choose or roll a dungeon kind.
2. Choose a size (short / standard / delve), which sets the room count.
3. Create rooms as graph nodes: always include entrance and goal, then fill the rest.
4. Connect them: a path from entrance to goal, plus branches and a few loops.
5. Label each connection with a passage or door type.
6. Give each room a size, a purpose drawn from the dungeon kind, and a contents result.
7. If the contents call for a trap or hazard, roll on the SRD-based trap table.
8. Add one or two dressing tags for atmosphere.
graphRules: Every map has exactly one entrance room and exactly one goal room.
Build a single path from entrance to goal that visits the listed number of intermediate rooms. The goal is at the end of this path.
Place the remaining rooms as branches: each branch room connects to one room already on the main path (not the entrance, unless the size is short).
Add the listed number of extra loop edges between already-placed rooms that are not already adjacent, so explorers can take a second route.
Do not connect the entrance directly to the goal.

rows.name: Stuck door
rows.suggestedCheck: DC 13 Strength (Athletics) to force, or 1 minute of noisy work

rows.name: Locked door
rows.suggestedCheck: DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with thieves' tools, or force DC 18

rows.name: Secret door
rows.suggestedCheck: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) to notice; opens by a visible catch once found

rows.name: Stairs or steep slope
rows.notes: Changes elevation by one level. If rolled on a loop edge, treat as an unlocked door instead.

rows.name: Rubble, portcullis, or collapse
rows.suggestedCheck: DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or a suitable tool/spell to clear; noisy

rows.name: Split level or gallery
rows.approxFeet: 30 x 30 with a ledge or pit

roomPurposes.notes: Roll 1d8 on the list for this dungeon kind. The entrance is always a threshold (gate, cave mouth, stairhead). The goal is always the last entry of the kind's list, or a rolled purpose marked as a fitting climax.

caves: Air shaft to the surface or a deeper dark (goal)
prison: Escape tunnel or the prisoner's cell (goal)

contents.notes: Original distribution meant to feel like a 5e adventure: plenty of empty or social space, a solid number of fights, and a minority of traps, puzzles, and loot. The entrance is usually empty or a weak watch. The goal is never empty: treat a roll of 1-6 as creature-with-treasure and a roll of 15-16 as a trap protecting the goal.

rows.name: Puzzle, locked barrier, or strange feature
Someone to talk to (prisoner, rival, denizen)

contents.encounterDifficultyHint: Size creature encounters with extras/encounterDifficultyA5e.json or 5.2/encounterBudgets.json. A standard adventure should mix mostly easy and medium fights, with the goal at hard.

trapsAndHazards.notes: Points at the SRD 5.2 example traps (5.2/traps.json, scaled by their At Higher Levels tables) and SRD 5.2 hazards. Rolling Stone is a levels 11+ trap; below that the engine uses a Collapsing Roof instead.

rows.name: Spiked Pit
rows.notes: Rare and deadly; if the party is below 7th level, reroll or treat as a pit.

rows.tag: A draft from somewhere you cannot see
Faint light (fungus, coals, a cracked door)
A sound that does not match this room (hammering, singing, dripping far off)
